title: Functorial K-injective resolutions with injective terms
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] and $\mathsf{Cpx}(\mathcal A)$ its category of cochain complexes and morphisms of complexes (defined as in [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] with $\mathcal A$ in place of $\Mod(\mathcal O)$). There are a functor $I:\mathsf{Cpx}(\mathcal A)\to\mathsf{Cpx}(\mathcal A)$ and a natural transformation $\eta:\mathrm{id}\Rightarrow I$ such that for every complex $K$: $\eta_K:K\to I(K)$ is a termwise monomorphism and a quasi-isomorphism, i.e. induces isomorphisms $H^n(K)\to H^n(I(K))$ of cohomology objects for all $n$ (as in [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules] with $\mathcal A$ in place of $\Mod(\mathcal O)$); $I(K)$ is K-injective, i.e. every morphism of complexes from an acyclic complex to $I(K)$ is homotopic to zero (as in [def-pur-kinjective-complex] with $\mathcal A$ in place of $\Mod(\mathcal O)$); and every term $I(K)^n$ is an injective object of $\mathcal A$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions].

source.place: Theorem 079P (theorem-K-injective-embedding-grothendieck), together with the injective-term clause in its construction

proof.text: Theorem 079P constructs the functor M that, for a chosen set of bounded-above acyclic complexes, sends every map from one of them to a null-homotopic map after a termwise monomorphic quasi-isomorphism. This is exactly [lem-pur-kinjective-functorial-homotopies].
The same construction supplies N, a functorial termwise monomorphic quasi-isomorphism through injective subobjects in every degree, as stated in [lem-pur-kinjective-functorial-injective].

The Baer argument in [lem-pur-kinjective-characterize-injective] identifies the lifting condition on subobjects of a generator with injectivity, and [prop-pur-kinjective-objects-small] makes maps from each term factor through an earlier stage of a sufficiently long transfinite chain.

The bounded-size acyclic complexes generated in the proof are detected by the criterion [lem-pur-kinjective-characterize-K-injective]: injective terms together with vanishing homotopy-category maps from those complexes imply K-injectivity.

Choose a cardinal $\kappa$ as in [lem-pur-kinjective-acyclic-quotient-complexes-bounded-size]; enlarging it keeps both clauses, so take $\kappa\ge\aleph_0$. By [lem-pur-kinjective-set-iso-classes-bounded-size] (2), applied termwise, choose a set $(K_i^\bullet)_{i\in I}$ of bounded-above acyclic complexes such that every bounded-above acyclic complex $P^\bullet$ with $|P^n|\le\kappa$ for all $n$ is isomorphic to some $K_i^\bullet$. Let $\mathbf M$ be the functor of [lem-pur-kinjective-functorial-homotopies] for this set and $\mathbf N$ the functor of [lem-pur-kinjective-functorial-injective]. Define functors $\mathbf T_\gamma$ with transformations $\mathrm{id}\Rightarrow\mathbf T_\gamma$ by transfinite recursion: $\mathbf T_0=\mathrm{id}$, $\mathbf T_{\gamma+1}=\mathbf N\circ\mathbf M\circ\mathbf T_\gamma$, and $\mathbf T_\lambda=\operatorname{colim}_{\gamma<\lambda}\mathbf T_\gamma$ (termwise) for limit $\lambda$. The transition maps are termwise monomorphisms and quasi-isomorphisms by those two lemmas; since filtered colimits in $\mathcal A$ are exact (AB5), each $K\to\mathbf T_\gamma(K)$ is again a termwise monomorphism and a quasi-isomorphism (elementary, Stacks 079P). Fix a generator $U$ and an ordinal $\alpha$ whose cofinality is greater than $\max(\kappa,|U|)$, hence uncountable; set $I(K)=\mathbf T_\alpha(K)$. Injective terms: a subobject $M\subset U$ has $|M|\le|U|$ (its subobjects are subobjects of $U$), so by [prop-pur-kinjective-objects-small] a morphism $\varphi:M\to\mathbf T_\alpha^n(K)$ factors through $\mathbf T_\gamma^n(K)$ for some $\gamma<\alpha$, hence through the injective subobject of $\mathbf T_{\gamma+1}^n(K)=\mathbf N^n(\mathbf M(\mathbf T_\gamma(K)))$ given by [lem-pur-kinjective-functorial-injective] (2), and so extends to $U$; by [lem-pur-kinjective-characterize-injective] each $\mathbf T_\alpha^n(K)$ is injective. K-injectivity: let $w:P^\bullet\to\mathbf T_\alpha(K)$ with $P^\bullet$ bounded above, acyclic, $|P^n|\le\kappa$; then $P^\bullet\cong K_i^\bullet$ for some $i$. By [prop-pur-kinjective-objects-small] each $w^n$ factors through some stage $\gamma_n<\alpha$; as there are countably many $n$ and the cofinality of $\alpha$ is uncountable, one $\gamma<\alpha$ serves all $n$, and since the transition maps are monomorphisms these factorizations commute with the differentials, so $w$ factors through a morphism of complexes $P^\bullet\to\mathbf T_\gamma(K)$. By [lem-pur-kinjective-functorial-homotopies] (2) its composite into $\mathbf M(\mathbf T_\gamma(K))$, hence into $\mathbf T_\alpha(K)$, is homotopic to zero, so $w$ is homotopic to zero. Hence [lem-pur-kinjective-characterize-K-injective], whose hypotheses on $\kappa$ are the two clauses of [lem-pur-kinjective-acyclic-quotient-complexes-bounded-size], shows that $\mathbf T_\alpha(K)$ is K-injective. Thus $I=\mathbf T_\alpha$ with $\eta:\mathrm{id}\Rightarrow\mathbf T_\alpha$ satisfies every clause of the statement.
